quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Recommended because it blocks the wind.
Not safe because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not safe because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to other vehicles. A driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane without knowing you are there.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after one hour passes.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see everything you need to see safely.
Can be dangerous for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see everything you need to see safely.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see as well as you need to for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: To make sure other drivers see you, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in bad weather.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: The best way to make sure others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on all the time.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a dry surface when stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get across the surface faster.
Make bigger zigzags so other drivers see you.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over grooves or gratings, keep your speed steady and go straight across. Do not try to avoid the weave by turning side to side, as this is more dangerous.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for it to start moving.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If you drink only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect how well you ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect how well you ride.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. Do not ride if you have had any alcohol.

questions.question: A protective jacket should:

options.text: Be loose so it flaps in the wind.

questions.explanation: Riding gear should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it stops you from moving.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Should not be noticed by other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash. It should keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let all other traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only by the lead rider.
Not checked often because they distract riders.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, all riders should check their mirrors often. This helps you see the riders behind you and keeps the group together.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane helps a car driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this position?

options.text: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirror.
Wind can block the side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. It is better to ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will not help. They may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding, wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Good riding boots should cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they won't catch on anything. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good helmet is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: No matter what style helmet you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives you the most protection when it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, you should be visible, signal your intentions, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times while riding.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait until a signal lets you turn the way you want to go.

questions.question: Keeping space between you and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can follow other vehicles more easily.
You have more time to react if other drivers move suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react if other drivers move suddenly.
questions.explanation: Always keep space around your motorcycle. This gives you time to see hazards and enough room to move safely if you need to.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced by:
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries can happen at any speed. A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: At a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move your lane position to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your lane position to be more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes other drivers see you best.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first.
